context_requirements: Cells must express ACSL4 and/or other PUFA-lipid-remodeling enzymes to generate oxidizable phospholipids.
Cells must have low or inhibitable GPX4 activity or low glutathione/NADPH buffering to accumulate lipid peroxides.
Cells must have intact stress-responsive transcription (NFE2L2/KEAP1, ATF4, NF-kB) to show the transcriptional signature.
Cells with high baseline antioxidant capacity or low PUFA content may show weak or no response.
falsifiers: No consistent induction of oxidative-stress or NFE2L2 target genes (e.g., HMOX1, SQSTM1, TXN, GCLM, SLC7A11) at 6 h or 24 h in any responsive line.
No repression of lipid-peroxidation or ferroptosis-related genes (e.g., GPX4, ACSL4, ALOX5, LPCAT3) at 6 h or 24 h.
A response pattern indistinguishable from generic proliferation arrest or apoptosis without oxidative-stress-specific genes.
Strong transcriptional response in all nine lines with equal magnitude, which would suggest a non-specific cytotoxic effect rather than lipid peroxidase inhibition.
